title: Generative Artificial Intelligence for Personal, Academic, and Lesson Planning Purposes: Applications and Perceptions of Irish Pre-Service Primary Teachers
extended_summary:
This paper examines how Irish pre-service primary teachers use generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) and how that use relates to their perceptions of GenAI for lesson planning. The central question is whether personal and academic experience with GenAI influences views about its value, risks, and professional development needs in lesson planning.

The study is a questionnaire-based survey conducted as the first phase of an international design-based research collaboration between teacher education institutions in Ireland and Arizona. The sample included pre-service primary teachers in two programs at one Irish institution: Bachelor of Education students and Professional Master of Education students. Participants reported their GenAI use for personal, academic, and lesson-planning purposes, and their perceptions of opportunities, challenges, ethical concerns, and the need for professional development.

Findings show that GenAI use was still in an early stage, with ChatGPT the most commonly used tool and lesson-planning use less common than personal or academic use. Participants saw GenAI as time-saving and potentially helpful for better lesson plans, but they were less confident about the creativity, originality, and reliability of AI-generated plans. They also expressed concerns about over-reliance, possible negative effects on children’s learning, educational inequity, data privacy, and the need for transparency. Importantly, personal GenAI use was not significantly related to lesson-planning perceptions, while academic use was positively associated with perceived opportunities and professional development needs, and negatively associated with perceived challenges and ethical concerns. The paper concludes that teacher education should provide foundational training for beginners and more advanced, critically oriented training for those with academic GenAI experience.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's GPT-based conversational AI chatbot used for generating and refining text and providing assistance across tasks such as writing and planning.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper reports that most respondents who had used GenAI tools used ChatGPT the most, and ChatGPT was the predominant tool used for personal, academic, and lesson-planning-related purposes in the survey.

findings.finding_summary: In this correlational survey of n=100 Irish pre-service primary teachers, 60 participants reported using ChatGPT the most among GenAI tools. The study did not evaluate ChatGPT-specific effects on lesson planning quality or instructional practice; rather, ChatGPT was the most commonly named tool in respondents' GenAI use patterns.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a quantitative cross-sectional survey with descriptive statistics and Pearson correlations, not an experimental or quasi-experimental efficacy study. The evidence is useful for understanding perceptions and use patterns, but it does not establish causal effects of ChatGPT on teacher planning quality or instructional practice.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper reports no tool-specific effect sizes for lesson planning outcomes and no evidence of measurable positive or negative impact on teacher practice. Reported correlations concern prior academic use of GenAI broadly, with no direct performance outcome, so impact on the target outcomes is unclear.
